questions.question: Name the three approaches suggested by Robert Fisher.
questions.solution_html:
• Social Work View: Emphasizes practical engagement, empowerment, and
  • problem-solving within the community.
  • Issue-based Action: Focus on specific, solvable issues that unite the
  • community.
  • 1 mark
  • 1 mark
  • Participation: Encourages local involvement and ownership in the planning
  • process.
  • Concept of Community Organization
  • o A professional social work method that involves organizing people to
  • identify needs, plan actions, and mobilize resources.
  • Government Initiatives
  • o Community Development Programme (1952): Foundation of
  • participatory rural development.
  • o National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM): Promotes self-help
  • groups and women’s empowerment.
  • o Swachh Bharat Mission & MGNREGA: Encourage community
  • participation in sanitation and employment.
  • 2 marks
  • 12 marks
  • Approaches of Social Action
  •  Gandhian Approach: Non-violent, moral persuasion and constructive
  • work (e.g., Salt Satyagraha).
  •  Marxian Approach: Radical and confrontational, focusing on class
  • struggle and redistribution.
  •  Alinsky’s Approach: Pragmatic, power-based, and issue-oriented (e.g.
  • community campaigns in Chicago).
  • Advocacy
  •  Represents community interests and influences policy.
  •  Encourages rights-based approaches and resource mobilization.
  •  Example: Advocacy for the Right to Information (RTI) Act by civil society
  • groups.

questions.question: Mention one type of observation skill useful in social work practice.
questions.solution_html:
• community social work.
  •  Definition: Observation skills involve carefully watching and listening to
  • understand people and situations, while analytical skills involve interpreting the
  • information gathered to make informed decisions.
  •  Purpose: Observation helps identify visible behaviors or conditions (e.g., poor
  • sanitation), whereas analysis helps understand underlying causes (e.g., lack of
  • municipal services).
  •  Process: Observation is direct and sensory; analysis involves reasoning
  • comparison, and critical thinking.
  •  Example: A social worker observes low attendance in a women’s meeting
  • (observation) and analyzes that cultural restrictions or timing issues are the causes
  • (analysis).
  •  Outcome: Together, they help in accurate problem assessment and effective
  • intervention planning in community work.
